info.title: WIB Middleware API
info.description:
Backend API contract for the myAccount React SPA.
This middleware sits between the React frontend and the legacy Symfony 3.4 backend (asigurari.ro).

## Authentication
- **Login** returns either full tokens (access_token + refresh_token) or a pre_auth_token when 2FA is required.
- **Access tokens** are short-lived RS256 JWTs (15 min). Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Refresh tokens** are opaque strings (7-day TTL). Send in the POST body to `/api/auth/refresh`.
- **Pre-auth tokens** are short-lived JWTs (5 min, scope=pre_auth) used only for the 2FA verification step.

## Naming Convention
- **Request bodies**: snake_case for multi-word fields (e.g. `refresh_token`, `pre_auth_token`, `new_password`).
- **Response bodies**: camelCase (e.g. `accessToken`, `policyNumber`, `createdAt`).
- This is documented per-field in each schema. The frontend should follow these conventions exactly.

## Error Format
All errors follow this structure:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "MACHINE_READABLE_CODE",
    "message": "Human-readable description.",
    "details": { "field": ["Validation message."] }
  }
}
```
The `details` key is only present for `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses.

## Rate Limiting
Sensitive endpoints are rate-limited per IP. When exceeded, a `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` error is returned.

## Error Codes Reference
| Code | HTTP | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| INVALID_CREDENTIALS | 401 | Wrong email or password |
| INVALID_PASSWORD | 400 | Wrong current password (change/disable 2FA) |
| INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN | 401 | Expired or revoked refresh token |
| INVALID_RESET_CODE | 400 | Wrong or expired OTP code |
| INVALID_RESET_TOKEN | 400 | Wrong or expired reset token |
| INVALID_TWO_FACTOR_CODE | 400 | Wrong TOTP/email OTP code |
| TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED | 200 | 2FA step needed (returns pre_auth_token) |
| USER_ALREADY_EXISTS | 409 | Email or username already taken |
| ACCOUNT_LOCKED | 423 | Too many failed login attempts (30 min lockout) |
| TOO_MANY_REQUESTS | 429 | Rate limit exceeded |
| VALIDATION_ERROR | 422 | Request body validation failed (see details) |
| SAME_PASSWORD | 422 | New password same as current |
| INVALID_2FA_METHOD | 422 | Method must be "totp" or "email" |
| INVALID_PRE_AUTH_TOKEN | 422 | Invalid or expired pre-auth token |
| POLICY_NOT_FOUND | 404 | Policy not found or access denied |
| QUOTE_NOT_FOUND | 404 | Quote not found or access denied |
| NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND | 404 | Notification not found or access denied |
| REMINDER_NOT_FOUND | 404 | Reminder not found or access denied |
| SESSION_NOT_FOUND | 404 | Session not found or access denied |
| UNAUTHORIZED | 401 | Missing or invalid JWT |
| FORBIDDEN | 403 | Insufficient permissions |
| NOT_FOUND | 404 | Route not found |

post.description:
Authenticates the user via email + password. Handled by the `json_login` firewall.

**Without 2FA**: returns `access_token`, `refresh_token`, and a `user` summary.
**With 2FA enabled**: returns `requires_2fa: true`, a short-lived `pre_auth_token`, and the `two_factor_method`.
The client must then call `POST /auth/two-factor` with the pre-auth token and TOTP/email code.

Rate limited: 5 attempts/minute per IP.

get.description: Returns the RSA public key used for JWT signature verification. Used by the legacy Symfony 3.4 backend.

post.description:
Creates a new user account. If a matching legacy user is found by username, the account is automatically
linked and profile data (person, contact, address, company) is hydrated from the legacy system.

On success, returns tokens immediately (user is auto-logged-in).
Accepts both camelCase (`firstName`) and snake_case (`first_name`) for backward compatibility.

Rate limited: 10 registrations/hour per IP.

username.description: Derived from email prefix if omitted

post.description:
Second step of the login flow when 2FA is enabled. The client submits the pre-auth token
received from POST /auth/login along with the 6-digit TOTP or email OTP code.

On success, returns full `access_token` and `refresh_token`.

Rate limited: 5 attempts/5 minutes per IP.

Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access_token + refresh_token pair.
The old refresh token is consumed (single-use). If the token is invalid, expired,
or already revoked, returns 401.

**Preferred:** The refresh token is read from the HttpOnly `refresh_token` cookie
(set automatically by login/register/previous refresh).

**Backward compatible:** If no cookie is present, falls back to reading
`refresh_token` from the JSON request body.

Rate limited: 10 requests/minute per IP.

refresh_token.description: Opaque refresh token (only needed if not using HttpOnly cookies)

post.description: Revokes the current session's refresh token and session record. Requires a valid JWT.

Sends a 6-digit OTP to the user's email address. Always returns success even if the email
is not registered (to prevent email enumeration).

Rate limited: 3 requests/hour per IP.

200.description: OTP sent (or silently ignored if email not found)

message.example: If an account exists for this email, a reset code has been sent.

post.description:
Validates the 6-digit OTP sent via email. On success, returns a one-time `reset_token`
that must be used with POST /auth/reset-password.

Rate limited: 5 attempts/15 minutes per IP.

Sets a new password using the reset token obtained from POST /auth/verify-reset-code.
Revokes all existing refresh tokens for the user (forces re-login on all devices).

Initiates 2FA setup. For `method=totp`, returns a TOTP secret and provisioning URI (for QR code).
The client must then call POST /auth/2fa/confirm with a valid TOTP code to activate it.
For `method=email`, 2FA is enabled immediately using email-based OTP codes.

provisioningUri.description: otpauth:// URI for QR code generation

message.example: Email two-factor authentication has been enabled.

post.description: Verifies the first TOTP code to confirm the secret is set up correctly. After this call, 2FA is fully active.

Resends the 2FA email OTP code during the login flow. Requires a valid pre_auth_token
and only works when the user's 2FA method is "email".

Rate limited: 3 requests/10 minutes per IP.

message.example: A new verification code has been sent to your email.

422.description: Invalid pre-auth token or wrong 2FA method

post.description: Disables 2FA for the authenticated user. Requires current password for confirmation.

get.description:
Returns aggregated counts and highlights for the authenticated user:
- Policy totals, active count, breakdown by type, and policies expiring within 30 days
- Quote totals and pending count
- Notification totals and unread count
- Upcoming reminders (next 7 days, not done) and total count
Returns all notifications for the authenticated user, ordered by creation date (newest first).

patch.description: Marks a single notification as read.
Marks all notifications for the authenticated user as read in a single operation.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of the authenticated user's insurance policies. Supports filtering by status and type.
Returns full details for a single policy. Returns 404 if the policy doesn't exist or belongs to another user.

Streams the policy document PDF through the middleware.
The transactionId and fileId are available from the policy's transactionId and fileIds fields.
The fileId is one of the values from the policy's fileIds map (e.g. fileIds.policy_pdf).

The document is proxied through the middleware so that the legacy download URL is never
exposed to the client — only authenticated users can access documents.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: File ID from policy fileIds map

get.description: Returns sync state records for the user's policies.
Returns a paginated list of the authenticated user's insurance quotes. Supports filtering by active state and type.
Returns full details for a single quote. Returns 404 if the quote doesn't exist or belongs to another user.

post.summary: Get offer URL for a quote
post.description: Requests the offer/results page URL from the legacy system. The quoteInputParamsId is available from the sync states endpoint.

403.description: Quote does not belong to user

get.description: Returns sync state records for the user's quotes. Each record contains quoteInputParamsId needed for the offer-url endpoint.
Returns all reminders for the authenticated user.

post.description: Creates a new reminder with a title, date, and optional note.

put.description: Updates one or more fields of an existing reminder. All fields are optional.

get.description: Returns all active sessions for the authenticated user. Each session includes a `current` flag indicating which session belongs to the current request.

current.description: True if this is the requesting session

delete.description: Revokes all sessions except the current one (identified by the JWT session ID). Effectively logs out all other devices.
Revokes a specific session and its associated refresh token. Cannot revoke the current session (use POST /auth/logout instead).

get.description:
Polls the legacy system for data changes since the last sync.
Intended to be called by the frontend every 10 minutes while the user is active.
Returns a summary of what changed (new/updated policies and quotes).
Returns the authenticated user's full profile. Sensitive fields (email, phone, lastName) are partially masked.

active.description: Whether the account is active. False means the account has been deactivated (e.g. GDPR deletion request).

patch.description: Updates one or more profile fields. All fields are optional — only provided fields are changed.
Updates language and/or notification preferences. All fields are optional.

post.description:
Changes the authenticated user's password. Requires the current password for verification.
On success, revokes all other sessions (keeps the current session alive via X-Refresh-Token header).

Deactivates the authenticated user's account (GDPR, scenario 5). Legacy data is NEVER
touched — the legacy DB is the regulatory system of record. The middleware calls the
READ-ONLY evaluation endpoint POST /api/middleware/delete-user-data to obtain a flag
describing what it may delete on its OWN side, then acts only on the middleware DB:
  - quote sessions with NO backing policy (deletable) are removed;
  - all policies and policy-backed quote sessions are left fully intact;
  - the user record is KEPT and only marked inactive (active=false) — it is never
    deleted and no personal data is anonymized.

Because the account is deactivated (not deleted), the user can no longer log in and all
sessions/refresh tokens are revoked. Fail-safe: any quote session the legacy side could
not evaluate is never deleted.

deactivated.description: Account is now inactive; the user is logged out and cannot log in again

deletedCount.description: Quote sessions (without a policy) removed from the middleware

retainedCount.description: Policies kept intact per ASF requirements

email: This value is not a valid email address.

policySeries.description: Policy series prefix (e.g. POL, PAD, FAC)

comboId.description: Links home combo policies (pad + facultative) belonging to the same package

active.description: Whether the policy is currently active

quoteRef.description: Reference linking back to the originating quote

fileIds.description: Map of file_type to file_id from policy_details.file_ids. Use with GET /user/policies/download/{transactionId}/{fileId}

insuranceType.description: Home/pad system only. pad=PAD obligatoriu, facultative=facultativa

data.description: Structured data with product details and insured person info

product.description: System-specific product data (vehicle plate+vin for auto, address for home, destination+days for travel)

daysUntilExpiry.description: Computed days until endDate (negative if expired)

insuranceType.description: Home/pad system only. Derived from insurer_details insurance_type.

active.description: Whether the quote is still a valid/active offer

data.description: Structured data with product details and insured person info

product.description: System-specific product data (vehicle plate+vin for auto, address for home, destination+days for travel)

UserProfile.description: Full user profile (sensitive fields partially masked)

id.description: HMAC-SHA256 hash of user ID (opaque, consistent across requests)

Bearer.description: RS256 JWT access token (15 min TTL). Obtain via POST /auth/login or POST /auth/refresh.
